diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber's upstream router has not checked in for 7.4 hours, exceeding the danger threshold. The router management/heartbeat path is unavailable, although the ONU and customer service path are currently still operational.
evidence: The trigger is a stale router heartbeat of 7.4 hours; more than 4 hours is classified as danger.
The ONU is online and responding, with normal RX power of -20.61 dBm and normal TX power of 2.40 dBm.
The seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX remains around -20.6 dBm, TX remains around +2.3 dBm, distance is constant at 152, and TX bias stays within the healthy range.
All tested peer ONUs on EPON0/2 are online, so there is no ONU, splitter, PON-port, or shared optical fault.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP and has healthy CPU, memory, and temperature, ruling out an OLT failure.
The VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1062, RADIUS records are consistent, and the customer has an active session with recent traffic, so authentication and provisioning are not the cause.
The stale router heartbeat is therefore the only active fault indicated by the evidence.

remediation.action: Check the router's power, management interface, upstream reachability, and monitoring agent. Attempt out-of-band access and verify whether it is forwarding traffic. Restore or reboot the router if required, then confirm heartbeat recovery and review the event logs around the last check-in.

ground_truth.root_cause: The BNG TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 stopped checking in 7.4 hours ago. Customers behind it lost their sessions at the same moment. The optical plant is entirely unaffected: ONUs remain registered and are returning normal signal readings.
expected_reasoning: Router heartbeat is 7.4 hours stale, past the 4 hour danger threshold
The ONU is online with RX -20.6 and TX 2.4, both normal, and the live probe confirms it
Every peer on the port is also online with normal optical readings
OLT ping, SNMP and device metrics are all healthy
So the optical layer is working and the fault is not in the fibre plant
Sessions across customers on this router ended together 7.4 hours ago
Throughput fell to zero at the same moment while the ONUs stayed registered
Healthy ONUs with dead sessions is the router signature: the optical layer carries no traffic without the BNG
The blast radius follows the router, not the OLT, so every customer it serves is affected
distractors: ONU status is online everywhere, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The OLT health check reports healthy, which is correct but irrelevant
Optical readings are perfect, which points away from where the fault is
